main_text.l: bet, hoc est, Diabolu; & liberos redderet, quot quot metu mortis per omne vitam obnoxii erant servituti. 1. Pet. 1. v. 18. Sciatis vos non caducis rebus, argento & auro fuisse redemtos ex vana vestra conversatione, ex patrum traditionibus ac cepta: Sed pretiofo sanguine, utpote agni immaculati, & incontaminati, nempe Christi, Gal. 3. v. 13. Christus nos redemit ab execratione legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio; (scriptum est enim: Execrabilis quisquis pendet in ligno) ut in gentibus benedictio Abrahae exstet in Christo Jesu, utque promissum illum Spiritum accipiamus per fidem. 2. Timoth. 1. v. 10. Gratia patefacta nunc est per illustrem illum adventum Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi, qui & mortem abolevit, & Vitam in lucem produxit, ac immortalitatem per Evangelium. Hunc JESUM, hoc est, SERVATOREM dici declarat Angelus Gabriel, Matth. 1.

Quod servaturus sit populum suum a peccatis ipsorum, nempe, tum remissionem peccatorum nobis impetrando, tum ipsa peccata in nobis abolendo, denique loco aeterni supplicii beatam vitam nobis conferendo.
V. Servatorem hunc aeternam nobis salutem peperisse dicit Quaestio,

marginalia.note: f. Hic Ser- sator peperit nobis salutē[?]

page.notes: The right margin note reads in three short lines, "f. Hic Ser-", "sator peperit", "nobis salutē"; the last word is partly cut off and the note is set in a small italic face, so the readings are doubtful. The catchword "Meri" at the lower right is cut off; I read it as "Meri[?]". A bold number "233" in the top right corner appears to be a later mark or library number, not part of the printed page, so I left it out. The text on the left of the header line appears to be a fragment of an older printed page; the faint "CAPUT" at lower left is show-through and was left out. The "Hunc JESUM" line is printed with a capital J. The Latin passages are printed in italic and transcribed as such.
